items.stem: A cost that stays the same in total regardless of the level of activity is best described as a:

options.rationale: Correct: fixed costs remain constant in total over the relevant range.
Variable cost changes in total with activity.
A semi-variable cost has both fixed and variable elements.
Marginal cost is the cost of one additional unit.

items.explanation: Correct: fixed costs remain constant in total over the relevant range.

items.stem: Using the high-low method, which data points are used to estimate the variable cost per unit?

options.text: The highest and lowest activity levels
options.rationale: Correct: the high-low method uses the highest and lowest activity levels.

options.text: The highest and lowest total costs only
options.rationale: It is driven by activity levels, not by selecting on cost.

options.text: The average of all activity levels
options.rationale: Averaging is not the high-low method.

options.text: Only the most recent two periods
options.rationale: Recency is not the selection rule in high-low.

items.explanation: Correct: the high-low method uses the highest and lowest activity levels.

items.stem: Select TWO items that would be classified as prime cost in a manufacturing business.

options.rationale: Correct: direct materials are part of prime cost.
Correct: direct labour is part of prime cost.
Factory rent is a production overhead, not prime cost.
Administrative salaries are a period cost, not prime cost.
Office depreciation is a non-production overhead.
